scope: Source-specific editorial decisions for the 2026-09-27 expansion batch (the execution session's v6). Its own manifest, as with every batch: it amends no earlier review, and nothing here joins the eight-protocol matrix or shares a ranking with any other result. These are fixed CPU baselines; the batch contains no foundation-model and no LoRA/PEFT result. Three sources are published as aggregates and one as status only. One of the three was held for its consent statement until the maintainer read it the same day.

sources.name: Cattan PC/VR P300 · a BCI experiment in virtual reality and on a personal computer
sources.task: P300 target detection, calibrated on one display and tested on the other
sources.version: Zenodo record 2605205 (2019): all 42 EEG recordings of the 21 paired participants and Header.mat
sources.attribution: Grégoire Cattan, Anton Andreev, Pedro L. C. Rodrigues and Marco Congedo · Dataset of an EEG-based BCI experiment in Virtual Reality and on a Personal Computer, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.2605205; documentation arXiv:1903.11297.
sources.privacyReview: The documentation reports that all 21 participants gave written informed consent covering the experimental process, the data management procedures and the right to withdraw at any moment, and that the study was approved by the Ethical Committee of the University of Grenoble Alpes (Comité d'Ethique pour la Recherche Non-Interventionnelle). Only cohort aggregates are published: means and participant-bootstrap intervals. The per-person minimum, maximum, median and quartiles in the reviewed inputs are dropped, because with 21 people each of them is one person's score.

sources.name: YSU asynchronous SSVEP-BCI dataset
sources.task: Control versus non-control rejection with fixed CCA
sources.version: figshare 24906300 revision 3: the S01-S04 archives only, a four-person pilot of the 24-person release
sources.attribution: Jing Zhao, Qian Zhang, Xinrui Wang, Xueshuo Liu, Jiaxin Li, Fengjie Fan, Zhenhu Liang and Xiaoli Li · An EEG dataset for studying asynchronous steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) based brain computer interfaces, Brain-Apparatus Communication 3(1) (2024), doi:10.1080/27706710.2024.2418650; data at doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.24906300.v3.
sources.privacyReview: The data descriptor (section 2.1, Subjects) reports that before the experiment all 24 subjects thoroughly understood the experimental procedures and signed written informed consent, and that the study was reviewed and approved by the ethics committee of Qinhuangdao First Hospital. This project uses a four-person pilot of the release (the first four participant archives). Only pooled window counts are published. The per-participant ranges in the reviewed inputs are dropped: with four people, each bound is one person's rate.

sources.name: Stieger longitudinal BCI · one-person pilot
sources.reason: One person's eleven sessions were acquired, not the 62-person release. With one person, every score is that person's, which this site does not publish; the execution handoff also asks for no ranked score and no session table. What is published is that the loader and a chronological split work on this source, and how many trials meet the source's own eligibility rules.
sources.attribution: James R. Stieger, Stephen A. Engel and Bin He · Continuous sensorimotor rhythm based brain computer interface learning in a large population, Scientific Data 8, 98 (2021); data at doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.13123148.v1.
sources.consentBasis: The data descriptor states that all experiments were approved by the institutional review boards of the University of Minnesota and Carnegie Mellon University and that informed consent was obtained from all subjects (Europe PMC PMC8016873).
